description: Erection of pitched roof extension with front dormer and installation of 3nos. rear rooflights to facilitate loft conversion. Changes to front and side fenestrations and installation of 2nos. windows to ground floor rear elevation.
decision_conditions: It is considered that the overall design of the proposed development would be unacceptable. The combined visual impact of the excessive bulk at the roof level, the overly prominent front roof dormer which is out of character within the local area, and the increased height which is not subordinate to the original building or proportionate to the size of the application site would adversely impact the character and appearance of the local area. As such, the proposed development is considered to be of an unsympathetic and overly prominent design and scale that would harm the character and appearance of the existing dwelling and the surrounding area. The proposal is therefore contrary to Policy D3 of the London Plan (2021), Policies CS8 and DM10 of the Council's Core Strategy (2012), and the guidance set out in the Council's Residential Design SPD (2012).

Having regard to the siting, scale, and design of the development, it is considered that the proposal would likely give rise to material overbearing effects, material loss of light, and material impact to the privacy of neighbours by reason of overlooking. Insufficient information has been provided to indicate otherwise, and thus the proposed development is considered to be unacceptable. The proposal would therefore fail to safeguard the amenity of neighbouring occupiers, contrary to Policy D3 of the London Plan (2021), Policies CS8 and DM10 of the Council's Core Strategy (2012), and the guidance set out in the Council's Residential Design SPD (2012).

The proposed development would not meet the minimum requirement for floor-to-ceiling heights and would result in a smaller proportion of the gross internal area (GIA) having an adequate floor-to-ceiling height compared to the existing building. As such, the proposal would decrease the housing quality at the application site. Additionally, due to the existing conditions regarding private outdoor amenity space, the site is not suitable for a single occupant. Thus, the increase in GIA to accommodate two persons living at the application site would further exacerbate the adverse impacts of the existing inadequate standard of accommodation. The proposal therefore fails to provide a high-quality standard of accommodation, contrary to Policy D6 of the London Plan (2021) and Policy DM13 of the Core Strategy (2012).
